newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INTER SEEK RETURN TO FORM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER SEEK RETURN TO FORM.

text.p: Italian title challengers Internazionale badly need to get back on the winning trail when they face Udinese at home on Sunday.
Inter come into the game in third place, just five points behind leaders Juventus but still smarting from a 2-0 home loss to Bologna last Sunday.
That defeat highlighted a period of indifferent form which has seen the side pick up 11 out of a possible 27 points in nine games since mid-November.
Inter striker Maurizio Ganz, who is likely to replace 'flu-ridden Chilean Ivan Zamorano, acknowledged the importance of the game.
"Inter are a very unpredictable side...but we'd better be careful just now because if we lose another match on Sunday then we can say goodbye to the league title," Ganz said.
Team mate Giuseppe Bergomi, an experienced former international defender, said: "Frankly, at this point in the season (the halfway mark), I would have thought we'd have more points than this...
"Clearly Juventus are the side to beat. They've managed to limit the damages of a mini-crisis and are going well again"
Inter coach Roy Hodgson must decide between fellow Englishman Paul Ince and Dutchman Aron Winter in midfield.
Ince has missed three games through suspension but is expected to return in place of Winter alongside Swiss playmaker Ciriaco Sforza, Salvatore Fresi and Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff.
Marco Branca will partner either Ganz or Zamorano in attack.

Udinese are without striker Oliver Bierhoff, who scored twice for Germany in the Euro 96 final against the Czech Republic, Polish defender Marek Kozminski and Egyptian midfielder Hazem Emam, all injured.
Brazilian Amoroso, scorer of four goals in 12 games, replaces Bierhoff and joins Paolo Poggi in attack.
Giovanni Stroppa, who broke his leg during Udinese's 1-0 defeat by Inter on the opening day of the season last September, will be in midfield.
Udinese come into the game in 13th place, four points clear of the relegation zone, and will hope to defy a losing record at the San Siro where they last won a league game in November 1957.
